d23e ROUND 6 = 1 blocking, ROUND 7 = 2 blocking (both the same point). Round 8 launched. Converging, and CRUCIALLY rounds 6 and 7 had ZERO self-inflicted findings — the method change (grep the whole plan for every mention of a changed concept, instead of re-reading) is holding after four straight rounds where I caused a finding while fixing another.

ROUND 6 refuted MY OWN round-5 fix, correctly. I had written "ONE call site at the read covers every reachable path". FALSE, for two verified reasons: (a) config.py:469 does its own env read via _llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_MODEL", "model", DEFAULT_MODEL), so a model_classes-only warning is silent on every path that builds a config without invoking the fan-out; (b) THE DEEPER ONE — resolve_model:205-207 calls resolve_model_string(step or workflow or cfg.model), passing an ALREADY-RESOLVED STRING, where the value is indistinguishable from a config-table `model` key or a per-step `model:`. A warning there would fire FALSELY at operators who never set the env var. PROVENANCE EXISTS ONLY AT THE ENV READ. Rule now: the warning goes at EVERY env read and nowhere else — config.py:469 plus the new literal read in model_classes.py. Two sites, correct and free because emission is per-call. Added both-paths-separately tests plus a negative control (config-table `model` with the env var UNSET must emit NO warning) — that control is what forbids the resolve_model_string placement.

ROUND 7 found that _deprecations.py:75-79 asserts "This registry now holds ONLY these permanent renames: every remaining SCHEDULED (removable) surface has been removed in the pre-1.0 breaking passes" — so adding a _scheduled entry makes an in-tree comment FALSE, and the plan had not scoped correcting it. Now scoped.

AND INVESTIGATING IT CLOSED THE WINDOW QUESTION FOR GOOD — the one I have flipped TWICE. The registry states its own reason for those six at :71-73: they are "stable REBAR_-prefixed renames of established names" that "warned 'deprecated' historically, which was a contradiction — they are kept forever." That is a RENAME: same knob, better name, must never be removed. REBAR_LLM_MODEL is NOT a rename — it is a knob SUPERSEDED by a different interface, which is exactly what _scheduled exists for and what the two pre-1.0 breaking passes at :87-99 actually used and then drained. So THE SIX PRECEDENTS ARE PRECEDENT FOR RENAMES, NOT SUPERSESSIONS. My round-3 switch to _permanent was wrong twice over: it contradicted the parent AND miscategorised the change. This reasoning is now written into the plan and into the corrected comment so it cannot be re-litigated a third time. It also means the eb6e reinstatement stands as recorded.

ALSO APPLIED: the _llm_str PRECEDENCE nuance queued last firing. _llm_str is CLI > env > file > default and RETURNS EARLY on a CLI hit, so os.environ.get is never reached when --model wins. Chose WARN-WHEN-SET (check os.environ.get(...) is not None at the :469 call site): an exported deprecated variable is still a migration item even when a flag overrides it. Warn-when-env-WINS rejected — it cannot live inside _llm_str (serves ~a dozen vars) and at the call site would duplicate the precedence logic the plan already refuses to duplicate. Added the distinguishing test (--model AND env both set -> CLI wins, warning still fires); without it the two semantics are indistinguishable to the suite.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING: config.py:469 is the ONLY env read (:10/:195 are docstrings; :470 is a DIFFERENT var, REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER — easy to miscount), _llm_str really does call os.environ.get, and NO alias-resolver path exists. So the two-site rule is COMPLETE, not just better than one.
